summary: Mahukona Light, dated 1889 by Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett, marks a North Kohala sugar port on Hawai'i Island; the 1915 concrete tower is listed as active.

structures.note: Tapered from 12 ft to 3 ft across; five-sided lantern. Lighthouse Friends says the remains are just north of the present light.

structures.type: lens lantern on a white mast
structures.note: 51 ft east and 11 ft west of the old tower; shown 35 ft above the ground and 64 ft above the water (Lighthouse Friends).

22 ft (6.7 m) square pyramidal reinforced concrete tower. Rowlett gives 22 ft (6.5 m), which does not convert from 22 ft; Lighthouse Friends: twenty-two-foot concrete pyramidal tower. The record's 22.0 does not match either source.

access.note: Site open, tower closed (Rowlett; Lighthouse Friends). Reached by a short walk south from Mahukona Beach Park, off Highway 270. The USLHS place record reads 'Open to Public: No'.

corrections.why: 22 ft is 6.7 m. Rowlett's 6.5 m does not match its own 22 ft figure; the record's 22.0 appears to be feet entered as metres.
Rowlett lists the light as Active, with a focal plane of 64 ft (19.5 m) and a white flash every 4 s. No source read records a closure.

The Commissioner's 1915 list shows the light in commission on 30 June 1915, and the 1915 change added a new tower and flashing light rather than closing the station. If a 1915 end date applies, it may refer only to the 1889 tower; a human should check the Light List before removing the value.
Mojibake of the Hawaiian name; Rowlett spells it Māhukona.

notes_for_editor: Disagreements in the story: (1) first light: 1889 (Lighthouse Friends; Rowlett; the 1936 Bulletin's 'established prior to 1890') against 1904 (USLHS 'Year Established'). The 1904 date may reflect federal establishment, but no source says so, so the story gives both. (2) Status: the record's 'inactive' and 'deactivated 1915' against Rowlett's 'Active' and the 1915 Commissioner list. The story follows Rowlett. (3) Height: the record's 22.0 m against 22 ft (6.5 m) in Rowlett and Lighthouse Friends. (4) Focal plane: 75 ft (23 m) for the 1889 light; 64 ft (19.5 m) for the 1907 and 1915 lights. The record's conflict list (22.86 m and 64.0) is explained this way. (5) Elgin's role: archive 'Laborer', Lighthouse Friends 'head keeper', 1906 to 1912 in both. The archive role is used. (6) Wikidata's 'built 1899' is not supported by any source read; the 1889 tower is the earlier date. (7) The Wight letter, the 1889 build, the 1907 light and the 1915 tower rest on Lighthouse Friends alone. No newspaper or government copy of the 1889 letter was found. (8) Chronicling America, Hawaiian papers: 'Mahukona light' 1889-1891 and 1900-1916 returned no lighthouse pages. 'Mahukona' with 'light' 1889-1891 and 'Mahukona' with 'keeper' 1904-1915 returned shipping and marine lists. Two pages were read: a 1904 Pacific Commercial Advertiser page describes a telegraph or wireless 'Mahukona station' (not the lighthouse; not used), and a 1907 Evening Bulletin page of shipping arrivals (not used). (9) The 1915 Bulletin OCR reads Mahukona as 'Mahukolla'; matched by context. The 1915 Commissioner's OCR is clean. (10) The record's 'deactivated 1915' might refer to the old tower. A Light List check would settle it. (11) No storms, wrecks or rescues are sourced for this station; that chapter is omitted. (12) No keepers are named for 1889 to 1903 in any source read. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1915 Bulletin (PDF p. 15) was checked on its text layer only; the browser pane downloads the uslhs.org PDF instead of showing it, so no page image was read. The garbled 'Mahukolla' line sits in the oil-to-acetylene list between two other Hawaii Island lights (Kawaihae, Keahole Point). 22 ft is 6.7 m; the story uses 6.7 m. The 1936 Bulletin's 'Since 1904' federal-maintenance statement is offered as a possible explanation for the USLHS 1904 date, not as the cause. The USLHS 'Open to Public: No' disagrees with Rowlett and Lighthouse Friends on access; the story states both.
